name: Greg Gornik
headline: Mechanical engineering student at UCD, aiming for design engineering in Formula 1.
intro: I like owning the whole loop: setting the target, designing it in CAD, proving it in FEA and getting my hands on the build. On UCD Formula Student, I set the chassis stiffness target and helped redesign the car's battery container. Away from the car, I'm building a live F1 strategy display, and I've spent years in workshops keeping bikes on the road.

about: I'm a third-year Mechanical Engineering student at UCD with one ambition: to design and build high-performance components for motorsport.

That drive comes from my time on UCD Formula Student. I'm on the chassis team, and I've been heavily involved in our first full chassis redesign, including the framework we now use to set torsional stiffness targets from the suspension. Before that, I designed and optimised suspension mounts and worked with the powertrain team on the mechanical design of our 2026 accumulator. Formula Student has shown me what it's like to work under real constraints, designing for weight, cost, packaging, manufacturability and a strict timeline. I can't wait to keep learning and help build an even better 2027 car.
I'm currently looking for internships, or just advice from people already working in motorsport design, so feel free to get in touch.

strengths.title: Team Mechanic and Mountain Bike Officer, UCD Cycling
strengths.evidence: I travel with the team to all the major national races, maintaining the bikes and equipment and supporting the riders from the team car during stages. As Mountain Bike Officer, I've also organised a lot of social spins for the club, which has taught me a lot about the difficulties and opportunities that come with managing people.

strengths.title: Workshop Administrator, Cycle SuperStore
strengths.evidence: I spent three and a half years in the shop, starting in sales and then running the workshop admin, coordinating repairs between customers and our mechanics. That meant explaining technical problems in plain terms, managing expectations and keeping both sides happy. Seeing what came back through the workshop gave me a practical understanding of how parts fail, what makes them serviceable, and why reliability matters as much as performance.

strengths.title: Workshop Manager, UCD Formula Student
strengths.evidence: I keep the team's workshop organised and safe, with every tool tracked and maintained, and look after our workstations and software, including Ansys, OptimumK and IPG CarMaker.

strengths.title: 3rd Year Rep, Mechanical Engineering Society
strengths.evidence: I'm the link between the faculty, the society and the students in my year, which has made me a better communicator and team player.
